Polycab India Limited
October 15, 2026

Moderator: Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to the Polycab India Limited Q2 FY27 Earnings
Conference Call. As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode and there
will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need
assistance during the conference call, please signal an operator by pressing star then zero on
your touchtone phone. Please note this conference is being recorded.
I now hand the conference over to Mr. Niyant Maru, Chief Financial Officer, Polycab India
Limited. Thank you, and over to you, sir.
Niyant Maru: Thank you. A very good evening to everyone, and thank you for joining us. I hope all of you are
staying healthy and gearing up for the upcoming festive season. On this call, we shall discuss
the Q2 FY27 results, which were approved in the Board meeting held earlier today.
We will be referring to the earnings presentation, financial results, and financial statements,
which are available on the stock exchanges as well as on the investor relations page of our
website. Joining me today from the management team, we have our Joint Managing Director,
Mr. Nikhil Jaisinghani; and Head of Investor Relations, Aditya Nathany.
Let me now hand over the call to Nikhil for his comments. Over to you, Nikhil.
Nikhil Jaisinghani: Thanks, Niyant. Good evening, everyone. As we conclude the first half of FY27, I am pleased
to share that Polycab has delivered its highest ever quarterly and half-yearly revenue and
profitability. This performance underscores the resilience of our operating model and the
strength of disciplined execution across the organization.
The Wires and Cables business continues to deliver robust growth, supported by healthy demand
trends, strong market positioning, and consistent execution. The FMEG segment continued to
strengthen its growth trajectory and recorded its seventh consecutive profitable quarter.
Across the organization, we remain focused on execution excellence, translating strategic
priorities into tangible outcomes while building a stronger foundation for sustainable long-term
growth. Encouragingly, the initiatives under our strategic roadmap, Project Spring, are
progressing in line with plan and are already beginning to yield meaningful results, reinforcing
our confidence in both the strategy and our ability to execute it effectively.
As we look ahead, our priorities remain firmly anchored on sustaining growth momentum,
further enhancing our competitive advantages, and investing in innovation, talent, and
capabilities. With a strong foundation in place and clear strategic direction, we are well-
positioned to capitalize on emerging opportunities and create enduring value for all our
stakeholders.
With that, I would now like to hand over to Niyant.
Niyant Maru: Thank you, Nikhil. While the global macro environment remained volatile during the quarter,
we continue to believe that India remains one of the most compelling structural growth stories
globally.

Polycab India Limited
October 15, 2026
Page 3 of 19
Geopolitical tensions, elevated energy prices, higher global bond yields, and disruptions across
certain international shipping routes have created near-term uncertainty across markets.
However, India continues to navigate and grow, supported by strong domestic demand, healthy
investment activity, accelerating infrastructure creation, and increasing manufacturing
competitiveness.
The IMF, in its latest outlook, has raised India's growth outlook by 60 basis points despite higher
global energy prices, citing stronger economic momentum, robust services activity, and
sustained domestic demand. This confidence is reflected in the recent upward revisions to India's
growth outlook by several other global agencies. Domestically, GDP growth for Q1 FY 2027
came in at 7.8%, underscoring the resilience of the economy despite an increasingly uncertain
external backdrop.
Global monetary conditions remain tight as central banks continue to combat inflation, resulting
in higher policy rates and bond yields across major economies. In India, the Monetary Policy
Committee, MPC, unanimously raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5% and shifted the
policy stance from neutral to calibrated tightening, implying interest rate cuts are not anticipated
in the near term.
While the external environment remains challenging, India's strong domestic demand, robust
banking system, and sustained infrastructure investment continue to underpin the economic
resilience. What gives us confidence is the breadth of growth visible across the economy. GST
collections continue to remain healthy, growing by 15% year-on-year.
In July, August, government capital expenditure remained significantly at higher levels, and
bank credit growth continues to trend close to 15% to 20%. Power demand has remained robust,
reflecting healthy activity across industrial, infrastructure, and commercial sectors.
The focus on infrastructure development continues, which is reflected in the government capex
spend of INR 5.10 lakh crores during April to August 2026, implying an 18% year-on-year
growth. The government has also approved another INR1.9 lakh crores of capital outlay for
Green Corridor Phase 3, which includes evacuation of 135 gigawatts of renewable energy and
deployment of battery energy storage systems.
All of this signals strong economic activity in India over the medium to long term. These
structural growth drivers continue to reinforce the long-term opportunity outlined under the
Project Spring.
While the near-term inflationary pressures are surfacing due to macroeconomic situations, both
urban and rural demand continues to remain healthy, while government support measures are
expected to aid broader consumption growth going forward. Importantly, India's revenue base
remains predominantly domestic, which provides a degree of resilience in periods of global
uncertainty.
Continuing on the momentum, the company delivered yet another remarkable quarter of strong
performance, underpinned by healthy revenue growth and profitability. Our performance reflects

Polycab India Limited
October 15, 2026
Page 4 of 19
not only favorable demand conditions, but also the deliberate investments and strategic choices
made over the past several years.
The Wires and Cables business continues the positive momentum, leveraging its market
leadership and execution capabilities, while the FMEG business has outperformed the market
across categories, supported by a growing product portfolio and a wider customer reach.
The progress we have achieved is underpinned by strong execution across our strategic priorities
and continued investment in our growth platforms. We remain committed to operational
excellence, disciplined capital deployment, and creating greater value for our stakeholders and
customers across every touch point.
Looking ahead, we see significant opportunities across our markets. Our priority will be to
accelerate our growth initiatives, strengthen our brands, deepen distribution, and build the
innovation and talent ecosystem needed to support the next phase of expansion.
To sum up, our outlook remains unchanged. While commodity volatility, geopolitical
developments, and logistics-related disruptions may continue to influence individual quarters,
the structural drivers of the demand remain firmly intact and in place.
We remain focused on disciplined execution of our Project Spring strategy, strengthening our
market leadership position, and investing behind the significant long-term opportunities
emerging across infrastructure, energy transition, manufacturing, urbanization, and exports.
Now, we would like to update you with reference to the ongoing proceedings with respect to
Asier Metals that we have filed an appeal before the Honorable National Company Law
Appellate Tribunal, Principal Bench, New Delhi, and the Honorable NCLAT has stayed and
kept in abeyance the order of admission in its entirety, including that of it being a commercial
dispute of INR 2.79 crores to set aside the order of admission passed by NCLT and initiation of
the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process, CIRP, against the company.
The company had gone for an early hearing on October 15, which is today, and we are of
reasonable opinion that we have argued well on the hearing and are reasonably confident and
hopeful that we have a strong case with grounds on merits and the judgment will land in our
favour.
We continue to monitor the situation and follow the due process as per law to get this resolved
as quickly as possible. We do not expect any adverse or material impact on our financial or
business operations arising from the said situation.
I would now hand over to Aditya to take you through the financial performance for the quarter.
Aditya Nathany: Thank you, Niyant. For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, we delivered an exceptional
performance reflecting the strength of our diversified business portfolio, disciplined execution
and sustained demand across our end markets. Consolidated revenue grew by 53% year-on-year,
with all business segments contributing meaningfully to this growth momentum.

Polycab India Limited
October 15, 2026
Page 5 of 19
The company continued to maintain a strong operational performance during the quarter.
EBITDA increased by 39% year-on-year, while EBITDA margins expanded by more than 50
basis points sequentially to 14.4%, supported by a favourable business mix and continued focus
on operational efficiencies.
Profitability remained robust, with profit after tax reaching a record high of INR 9,900 million,
representing a 43% year-over-year increase. PAT margins stood at 10.0% for the quarter,
reflecting healthy earnings growth and sustained margin resilience. Our financial position
remains very strong.
Net cash stood at INR 45.2 billion as of September 30th, 2026, compared to INR 29.4 billion a
year ago. We also witnessed further improvement in our working capital efficiency, with the
average working capital cycle reducing to approximately 11 days in second quarter fiscal '27.
This was aided by higher payable days arising from the increased use of letters of credit for our
raw material procurement.
As these benefits gradually normalize, we expect the working capital cycle to trend towards our
long-term operating range of 45 to 50 days. During the first half of the year, we incurred capital
expenditures of INR 6.1 billion, reflecting our ongoing investments in capacity expansion,
supply chain capabilities and future growth platforms.
